title: An Overwhelming Success

source.title: Iranian 'ghost fleet' filmed evading US blockade en route to China, UANI says
source.note: published 11-01 19:28 EST (11-02 00:28 UTC); carried in the 11-02 sweep, matched on 'hormuz', 'strait of', 'tanker', 'petrol' (in 'petroleum'), 'sanction', 'iran' — the fullest match in the queue. Read in full via the cloud fetch as paragraph reductions (no quotation over ten words). 46 body paragraphs: the article and one source — Jemima Shelley, senior analyst at United Against Nuclear Iran (an advocacy organisation; its own film is the page's evidence) — reported, stationed with the publication. No holder on the page: CENTCOM was asked and had not answered; Trump is not mentioned in the body. Chosen as the only RI-corner page in the queue on the water (The Close and the three Bloomberg feeds 0 items); my call

object.label: H6 — the Strait of Hormuz (PG01, the water), read from the lock's end: the US naval blockade of Iran's ports — begun 13 April, lifted mid-June, reinstated 14 July after talks collapsed (¶15) — read by an advocacy group's analyst as 'an overwhelming success' (¶16): no Iranian crude out since July (¶17), nine small tankers through (¶2, ¶7), one of them filmed (the SOGL, 500,000 barrels of LPG, Assaluyeh → the Strait → a ship-to-ship transfer in the Gulf of Oman → a Malaysian anchorage 70 km offshore → Xinzhou, China; ¶3–¶5, ¶26, ¶43); Iran's floating storage drained to 0–7 million barrels (¶35); China taking nearly all of Iran's oil and LPG (¶40). The blockade is the condition Iran sets for reopening the Strait (the NYT hed and the AP wire the same day); the page reads it as a victory. The pump, the price, the deal and the holder are not on the page

zAxis.pos: the water reopens — transits restored for every buyer, the blockade lifted or moot, the deal's cure reaching the pump
zAxis.neg: the water stays locked from both ends — Iran's ports blockaded, Iran's exports to one buyer through a leak, the shortfall held

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's 'U.S. control' of the water (the Strait reopened, 'continues to claim', msnow 10-15) and the deal as the cure. This page has the control claim in its most literal form — the lock from Washington's end, dated and sized — and reads it as success: the measure of success is zero Iranian crude on the water, which is the supply the pump is missing. The page never says so. The leak it films (nine small LPG tankers to China via Malaysia) is the only flow on the page, and it goes to one buyer. On the same day the holder's office tells Al Jazeera that Gulf flows exceed pre-conflict levels, and Iran offers (NYT hed) to reopen the Strait in two days if, among other things, the blockade is lifted. Read as my call: a blockade that holds is the water locked from the second end — negative on the price's Z — whatever the page calls it

operative.label: the US maritime blockade of Iran's ports: begun 13 April, lifted mid-June, reinstated 14 July after talks collapsed; Iran's crude exports largely stopped (¶15) — the fullest dating of the lock on the Press
UANI: at least nine small oil or LPG tankers through the blockade since July (¶2, ¶7); no Iranian crude out since reinstatement (¶17); floating storage down to 0–7 million barrels (¶35)

the SOGL (IMO 9208227; Comoros and Zimbabwe flags; Gravion Maritime): ≈500,000 bbl of LPG loaded at Assaluyeh in late August; through the blockade 1 September; filmed bunkering at the Malaysian EOPL anchorage (≈70 km offshore) on/after 16 September; discharged at Xinzhou, China; added to the OFAC list 8 October (¶3–¶5, ¶12–¶14, ¶29–¶30, ¶43)
the route: load in the Persian Gulf → transit the Strait of Hormuz → ship-to-ship transfer in the Gulf of Oman → the receiving tanker breaches the blockade (¶26–¶27); AIS off, false flags (¶24)
China: 80% of Iran's liquid cargo exports before the war, now nearly all of its oil and LPG (¶40); the G Summer (≈7,000 m³ LPG) tracked in April beyond the blockade line (Bloomberg, ¶44)
